Table is empty, so column meanings cannot be confirmed from data; the schema is consistent with Neutron's qos_policies (id, name, description, tenant_id/project_id, shared, is_default, standard_attr_id), but the four observed VARCHAR columns cannot be mapped to specific fields with confidence.

table.name: qos_port_policy_bindings
table.purpose: Neutron QoS extension table binding ports to QoS policies (which port uses which QoS policy). Table is empty (0 rows), so meaning is inferred from the table name and the surrounding Neutron schema (qos_policies, qos_network_policy_bindings, ports), not from data.

col_001.name: port_id
col_001.description: UUID of the port bound to a QoS policy. No data present; inferred from the table name (port-policy binding) and the standard Neutron qos_port_policy_bindings schema, where the two columns are port_id and qos_policy_id. Which of the two columns is port_id vs policy_id cannot be determined from the data itself.

col_002.name: qos_policy_id
col_002.description: UUID of the QoS policy applied to the port (references qos_policies). No data present; inferred from the table name and the standard Neutron schema. Column order (port_id first, qos_policy_id second) is assumed and could be reversed.

table.name: qospolicyrbacs
table.purpose: RBAC (role-based access control) entries controlling which tenants can access QoS policies. The table name and the surrounding OpenStack Neutron schema (qos_policies, networkrbacs) strongly suggest this, but the table is empty (0 rows) and no column names or join evidence are provided, so the table meaning itself is tentative and every column is unresolved. In the standard Neutron schema this table has columns id, object_id (QoS policy UUID), target_tenant, action, and tenant_id, which matches the count of five VARCHAR columns, but this cannot be confirmed from the data.

table.name: qosqueues
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron QoS queue definitions (legacy QoS extension): named queues with minimum and maximum bandwidth rates and DSCP marking, attachable to networks (see networkqueuemappings) and ports (portqueuemappings). Table is empty, so column meanings are inferred from the Neutron schema and sibling tables, not from data.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: UUID primary key of the QoS queue. No data to confirm; inferred from Neutron schema convention.

col_002.name: network_id
col_002.description: UUID of the network this queue is bound to (joins to networks / networkqueuemappings). No data to confirm.

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Human-readable name of the queue. No data to confirm.

col_004.name: default
col_004.description: TINYINT flag indicating whether this is the default queue. No data to confirm.

col_005.name: min
col_005.description: Minimum guaranteed bandwidth rate (kbps) for the queue. No data to confirm units.

col_006.name: max
col_006.description: Maximum bandwidth rate (kbps) for the queue; 0 typically means unlimited. No data to confirm units.

col_007.name: qos_marking
col_007.description: QoS marking type, expected values 'dscp' or 'trusted'. No data to confirm.

col_008.name: dscp
col_008.description: DSCP value (0-63) applied when qos_marking is 'dscp'. No data to confirm.

table.name: quotas
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron per-tenant resource quota limits: one row per (tenant, resource type) specifying the maximum number of that resource the tenant may create (-1 = unlimited).

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: UUID primary key uniquely identifying the quota record.

col_002.name: tenant_id
col_002.description: Tenant/project ID (32-hex OpenStack-style identifier) the quota applies to; each tenant has one row per resource type.

col_003.name: resource
col_003.description: Neutron resource type the quota limits, e.g. network, subnet, port, router, floatingip, security_group_rule.

col_004.name: limit
col_004.description: Maximum allowed number of the resource for the tenant; -1 means unlimited.

table.name: quotausages
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron per-project quota usage tracking: for each tenant (project) and resource type, the number of resources in use and reserved against the tenant's quota (companion to the 'quotas' and 'reservations' tables).

col_001.name: project_id
col_001.description: Tenant/project identifier (32-char hex UUID without dashes). Joins to default_security_group's tenant column; each project has multiple rows, one per resource type.

col_002.name: resource
col_002.description: Neutron resource type being counted against quota: port, security_group, network, subnet, router, security_group_rule, floatingip, etc.

col_003.name: dirty
col_003.description: Flag indicating the usage count is stale and needs recalculation (Neutron's 'dirty' marker on quota usage rows). Alternative reading: it could mark rows pending quota reservation commit, but the dirty-marker interpretation fits Neutron's quota usage design best.

col_004.name: used
col_004.description: Number of resources of the given type currently in use by the project (mostly small counts, max 602).

col_005.name: reserved
col_005.description: Number of resources reserved (held by in-flight operations) but not yet used; always 0 in this data, matching Neutron's typically-unused reservation mechanism. Alternative reading: it could be a general-purpose counter, but the companion 'reservations' table and the used/reserved pairing support the reservation interpretation.

table.name: reservations
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron quota reservation table: each row records a temporary reservation of resources against a project (tenant), created when an operation needs to hold quota until it completes or expires. The 32-hex project id and UUID/timestamp pattern match Neutron's quota/reservation engine (alongside the quotas, quotausages and resourcedeltas tables).

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key; UUID uniquely identifying the reservation.

col_002.name: project_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the project (tenant) on whose behalf the resources are reserved. 32-character hex string without dashes, consistent with a Keystone project/tenant ID. Constant across the 5 sample rows, i.e. all reservations belong to one project.

col_003.name: expiration
col_003.description: Timestamp when the reservation expires (reservations are short-lived; the values span a few days in April 2019). Could alternatively be a creation timestamp, but in Neutron's reservation table this column is the expiration time.

table.name: resourcedeltas
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron's resourcedeltas table: per-resource usage deltas attached to a quota reservation (created when quota is reserved, e.g. for concurrent port creation). Each row records one resource type and the amount of change for a specific resource ID under a reservation. In upstream Neutron the columns are resource, resource_id (UUID), and reservation_id; here the reservation link is not visible, so the table is inferred from the Neutron schema and the 'port' resource values.

col_001.name: resource
col_001.description: Type of Neutron resource being reserved/counted. All sampled rows are 'port', matching Neutron port-creation quota reservations; other values (e.g. 'subnet', 'network', 'floatingip') would appear for other operations.

col_002.name: resource_id
col_002.description: UUID of the specific resource instance the delta applies to (e.g. the port being created). Primary key of this table. It does not join to other tables here because the referenced rows (e.g. in ports) may not exist yet at reservation time.

col_003.name: delta
col_003.description: Signed integer change in resource count for this reservation; 1 means one unit of the resource is being reserved. All sampled rows are 1, consistent with reserving one new port.

table.name: router_extra_attributes
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron extension table holding extra (plugin-specific) attributes for routers: HA/distributed mode flags, HA virtual router ID, and availability zone hints. One row per router, keyed by router UUID.

col_001.name: router_id
col_001.description: UUID of the router this row extends; primary key, referenced by routerports and floatingips (which point back to routers).

col_002.name: distributed
col_002.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the router is a distributed (DVR) router; always 0 (false) in this data, so the reading rests on the table's known schema rather than observed variation.

col_003.name: ha
col_003.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the router is an HA router; always 0 (false) in this data, so the reading rests on the table's known schema rather than observed variation.

col_004.name: service_router
col_004.description: Boolean flag, always 0. In Neutron this column is 'service_router' (service-type router flag); evidence is weak since all values are false.

col_005.name: ha_vr_id
col_005.description: Nullable integer; in Neutron this is the HA virtual router ID (VRID) allocated for HA routers, null when the router is not HA. All non-null values are 0 here, so the exact meaning is not fully confirmed.

col_006.name: availability_zone_hints
col_006.description: JSON-encoded list of availability zone hints for scheduling the router; '[]' means no hints, null when unset.

table.name: routerl3agentbindings
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron table binding routers to L3 agents: each row records that a router (col_001) is scheduled on a particular L3 agent (col_002). With only one distinct agent value, all 27 routers are hosted on the same single L3 agent in this deployment.

col_001.name: router_id
col_001.description: UUID of the router being bound to an L3 agent. Primary key of this table; referenced by routerports.col_001 (router_id) and floatingips.col_008, confirming it identifies a router.

col_002.name: l3_agent_id
col_002.description: UUID of the L3 agent hosting the router. All 27 rows share one value, consistent with a single L3 agent serving all routers; the table name and the presence of an 'agents' table support this reading, though no direct join evidence confirms it.

table.name: routerports
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron router-to-port attachment table: each row links a router to a Neutron port, distinguishing gateway ports from internal interfaces. (In stock Neutron this table also has a port_type column; here the type is stored in col_003.)

col_001.name: router_id
col_001.description: UUID of the router (references routers.id). Multiple rows can share the same router (e.g. one gateway plus several interfaces), hence 22 distinct routers across 35 rows.

col_002.name: port_id
col_002.description: UUID of the Neutron port attached to the router (references ports.id); primary key of this table, unique per row.

col_003.name: port_type
col_003.description: Type of router attachment: 'network:router_gateway' (the router's external gateway port, 15 rows) or 'network:router_interface' (an internal interface to a subnet, 20 rows).

table.name: routerroutes
table.purpose: Empty table in an OpenStack Neutron database. Given the name and sibling tables (routers, routerrules, routerports, subnetroutes), this is plausibly Neutron's extra route storage for routers (e.g., destination CIDR / next-hop pairs), but the table has zero rows and no join metadata, so its exact semantics cannot be confirmed from the data. The three VARCHAR columns are unresolved; in Neutron's schema such tables typically hold a router UUID, a destination CIDR, and a next-hop IP, but that reading is not supported by evidence here and is not even offered as tentative per-column since nothing distinguishes the columns from one another.

table.name: routerrules
table.purpose: Likely per-router routing rules in an OpenStack Neutron database (related tables: routers, routerroutes, routerports). However the table is empty (0 rows), so its exact semantics cannot be confirmed from data. In Neutron this table historically stored Cisco CSR 1000V router 'extraroute' rules (source/destination CIDR, action, next-hop) for the Cisco L3 routing plugin, which fits the presence of cisco_csr_identifier_map and cisco_router_mappings in the schema. Marked tentative because no rows exist to verify against. Each row would represent one routing rule attached to one router.

table.name: routers
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron virtual routers: one row per logical L3 router instance owned by a tenant/project, with its name, lifecycle status, admin state, and gateway port reference. Referenced by routerports, floatingips, and other router-related tables.

col_001.name: tenant_id
col_001.description: Owner tenant/project ID (32-hex OpenStack project identifier). References the tenant of the default security group, i.e. the project that owns this router.

col_002.name: id
col_002.description: UUID primary key of the router. Referenced by routerports (router interfaces) and floatingips (router_id of the router a floating IP is associated with).

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Human-readable display name of the router (e.g. 'blitz', 'orbit', 'comet_delta'). Not unique.

col_004.name: status
col_004.description: Lifecycle/provisioning status of the router; all rows are 'ACTIVE' in this data, but the column is a status code (ACTIVE, e.g. also BUILD/ERROR in Neutron).

col_005.name: admin_state_up
col_005.description: Administrative state flag: 1 = router is administratively enabled/up. All rows are 1 here.

col_006.name: gw_port_id
col_006.description: UUID of the router's external-network gateway port (references ports.id, seen via routerports/ml2_port_bindings). Null for ~44% of routers, i.e. routers with no external gateway configured.

col_008.name: standardattributes_id
col_008.description: Foreign key to standardattributes, the shared table holding generic metadata (description, timestamps, tags, revision numbers) for Neutron resources.

table.name: securitygroupportbindings
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron many-to-many association table binding security groups to ports (which security groups are applied to which networking ports).

col_001.name: port_id
col_001.description: UUID of the network port (references ports.id). A port can appear in multiple rows, once per security group applied to it.

col_002.name: security_group_id
col_002.description: UUID of the security group (references securitygroups.id). One security group can be bound to many ports.

table.name: securitygrouprules
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron security group rules: each row is a single allow-rule (direction, protocol, port range, remote source) attached to a security group.

col_001.name: tenant_id
col_001.description: Project/tenant identifier (32-char hex, no dashes) that owns the rule; references default_security_group's tenant column.

col_002.name: id
col_002.description: UUID primary key of the security group rule.

col_003.name: security_group_id
col_003.description: UUID of the security group this rule belongs to (references securitygroups.id).

col_004.name: remote_group_id
col_004.description: UUID of a remote security group whose members are allowed as source/destination; null when the rule uses a CIDR instead. Also matches securitygroups.id.

col_005.name: direction
col_005.description: Traffic direction the rule applies to: 'ingress' or 'egress'.

col_006.name: ethertype
col_006.description: IP version of the rule: 'IPv4' or 'IPv6'.

col_007.name: protocol
col_007.description: IP protocol: tcp, udp, icmp, or an IP protocol number (41 = IPv6 encapsulation, 47 = GRE); null means all protocols.

col_008.name: port_range_min
col_008.description: Lower bound of the destination port range (0-65535); null when not applicable (e.g. icmp or all protocols).

col_009.name: port_range_max
col_009.description: Upper bound of the destination port range (0-65535); null when not applicable.

col_010.name: remote_ip_prefix
col_010.description: Source/destination CIDR allowed by the rule (e.g. 10.71.29.205/8); null when remote_group_id is used instead.

col_011.name: standard_attr_id
col_011.description: One-to-one reference to standardattributes, holding shared metadata (timestamps, revision, etc.) for the rule.

table.name: securitygroups
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron security groups: named sets of firewall rules applied to ports, scoped per project/tenant. Referenced by securitygrouprules and securitygroupportbindings; each project has a default security group (default_security_group).

col_001.name: project_id
col_001.description: Project/tenant identifier (32-char hex UUID without dashes). References default_security_group, which tracks each project's default security group. The top value 'aurum-xenon' project owns 83 groups.

col_002.name: id
col_002.description: UUID primary key of the security group. Referenced by securitygrouprules (as security_group_id and remote_group_id) and by securitygroupportbindings.

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Human-readable name of the security group. 'aurum-xenon' (804 rows) is the auto-generated default security group name for the dominant project; others are user-chosen names.

col_004.name: standard_attr_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to standardattributes, the shared table holding standard resource metadata (created_at, updated_at, description, revision number, tags). One-to-one.

table.name: serviceprofiles
table.purpose: Almost certainly the OpenStack Neutron 'serviceprofiles' table: definitions of service profiles that can be attached to network flavors (see the companion tables 'flavors' and 'flavorserviceprofilebindings'). The column meanings below are tentative for the same reason: no values, no primary key detection, and no joins were observed to confirm them. The pattern of three VARCHAR columns plus one TINYINT plus one VARCHAR matches Neutron's documented schema (id, description/driver, metainfo, enabled), but the exact column-to-name mapping cannot be verified from the evidence provided.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Plausibly the UUID primary key of the service profile (Neutron uses VARCHAR(36) UUIDs). No primary key was detected and the table is empty, so this cannot be confirmed; it could equally be the 'driver' or 'description' column.

col_002.name: driver
col_002.description: Plausibly the driver/provider name for the service profile (e.g. a neutron advanced-service driver string). No values exist to confirm this, and it could also be 'description' or 'metainfo'.

col_003.name: metainfo
col_003.description: Plausibly free-form metadata string for the profile. No data to confirm; could be 'description' or 'driver' instead.

col_004.name: enabled
col_004.description: The only TINYINT column, matching Neutron's 'enabled' boolean flag for service profiles. The boolean role guess supports this, but with zero rows there is no value evidence.

col_005.name: description
col_005.description: Plausibly a free-text description. No data to confirm; the assignment among the VARCHAR columns is guesswork.

table.name: lbaas_sessionpersistences
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron LBaaS v2 session persistence configuration for a load balancer pool. Each row stores the session persistence type (SOURCE_IP, HTTP_COOKIE, or APP_COOKIE) for one pool, keyed by pool_id. With type HTTP_COOKIE, no cookie name is needed; with APP_COOKIE, a cookie name would be set. The single row here configures HTTP_COOKIE persistence for one pool. This appears to be the v1-style 'sessionpersistences' table (companion to 'pools'/'vips'), distinct from 'lbaas_sessionpersistences' which pairs with 'lbaas_pools'. The evidence for which pool table it belongs to is not conclusive from the data alone, so the table-level linkage is tentative; the column meanings are clear from the Neutron schema and values.

col_001.name: pool_id
col_001.description: Primary key; UUID of the load balancer pool this session persistence setting belongs to. In the Neutron schema this table is keyed by the pool's id (one session-persistence row per pool).

col_002.name: type
col_002.description: Session persistence type. Observed value 'HTTP_COOKIE' (persistence via an HTTP cookie injected by the load balancer). Other allowed values in Neutron are 'SOURCE_IP' and 'APP_COOKIE'.

col_003.name: cookie_name
col_003.description: Name of the application cookie used for persistence; only applicable when type is APP_COOKIE. Null here because the type is HTTP_COOKIE, which requires no cookie name. The all-null column gives no direct value evidence, but the Neutron schema and the HTTP_COOKIE row support this reading.

table.name: standardattributes
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron 'standardattributes' table: a shared registry of common metadata (timestamps, revision tracking) for all Neutron resources (networks, subnets, ports, security groups and rules, routers, floating IPs, etc.). Each row represents one Neutron resource; other tables reference it by id to attach standard attributes. The resource type is stored here, and the specific resource tables (networks, ports, securitygrouprules, ...) join one-to-one on their standard-attribute id column, matching the observed referenced_by joins.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate id of the standard-attributes record. Referenced one-to-one by the standard-attribute id columns of resource tables (securitygrouprules, ports, securitygroups, floatingips, routers, subnets, networks, ...), i.e. each row identifies exactly one Neutron resource.

col_002.name: resource_type
col_002.description: Type of the Neutron resource this row describes; values are the resource table names: securitygrouprules, ports, securitygroups, networks, subnets, routers, floatingips.

col_003.name: created_at
col_003.description: Creation timestamp of the resource. Null for ~29% of rows (older records predating this column's introduction).

col_004.name: updated_at
col_004.description: Last-update timestamp of the resource. Null for ~27% of rows (never updated or predating the column).

col_005.name: description
col_005.description: Free-text description of the Neutron resource, stored in the shared standard-attributes record. This is the only free-text column here, and the joined referencing tables (ports, securitygroups, floatingips, routers, subnets, networks) all document that standardattributes carries a shared 'description' field alongside timestamps and revision numbers.

table.name: subnetpoolprefixes
table.purpose: Likely stores the address prefixes (CIDRs) belonging to each subnet pool in an OpenStack Neutron database, given the companion 'subnetpools' table and Neutron's known schema. However, the table is empty (0 rows) and column names are opaque, so this is tentative rather than confirmed by data. Each row would represent one CIDR prefix assigned to a subnet pool. The two columns likely correspond to Neutron's standard 'prefix' (the CIDR string) and 'subnetpool_id' (foreign key to subnetpools), but the evidence does not distinguish which column is which, so both are left unresolved.

table.name: subnetpools
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron subnet pool definitions: pools of CIDR prefixes from which subnets can allocate addresses (table is empty; inferred from the surrounding Neutron schema, e.g. subnetpoolprefixes, subnets, address_scopes).

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: UUID primary key of the subnet pool (Neutron convention; VARCHAR(36)).

col_002.name: name
col_002.description: Human-readable name of the subnet pool.

col_003.name: tenant_id
col_003.description: Owning project/tenant identifier (Neutron convention; could alternatively be address_scope_id, but tenant_id typically precedes it).

col_004.name: ip_version
col_004.description: IP version the pool serves (4 or 6).

col_005.name: default_prefixlen
col_005.description: Default prefix length (bits) for subnets created from this pool.

col_006.name: min_prefixlen
col_006.description: Minimum allowed prefix length (bits).

col_007.name: max_prefixlen
col_007.description: Maximum allowed prefix length (bits).

col_008.name: shared

col_009.name: default_quota
col_009.description: Default per-tenant quota of IP addresses usable from the pool.

col_010.name: address_scope_id
col_010.description: FK to address_scopes.id; scope in which the pool's prefixes live.

col_011.name: is_default
col_011.description: Whether this is the default pool for its IP version (stored as string boolean in some Neutron versions).

col_013.name: standard_attr_id
col_013.description: FK to standardattributes.id, carrying shared metadata (created_at, description, revision number, tags).

table.name: subnetroutes
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron host routes (extra routes) attached to subnets: each row is a static route (destination CIDR via a next-hop IP) for a given subnet.

col_001.name: destination
col_001.description: Destination CIDR of the route, in IP/prefix notation (e.g. 10.169.77.216/8). The /8 prefix on host-like addresses suggests synthetic/test data, but the column is clearly the route destination network.

col_002.name: nexthop
col_002.description: Next-hop (gateway) IP address in CIDR notation for reaching the destination, e.g. 10.30.19.197/8.

col_003.name: subnet_id
col_003.description: UUID of the subnet this route belongs to; references subnets (its id column).

table.name: subnets

col_001.name: tenant_id
col_001.description: Owning project/tenant identifier (32-char hex, no dashes). References default_security_group's tenant/project column; several subnets share a tenant.

col_002.description: Primary key: UUID of the subnet. Referenced by ipallocationpools, ipallocations, dnsnameservers, subnetroutes, lbaas_loadbalancers and lbaas_members.

col_003.description: Human-readable subnet name (e.g. 'dash_spark', 'spike_drive', 'xenon9'); mostly unique but not enforced.

col_004.name: network_id
col_004.description: UUID of the parent network (references networks.id); a network can host multiple subnets.

col_005.name: ip_version
col_005.description: IP version of the subnet: 4 (IPv4) for 47 rows, 6 (IPv6) for 2 rows.

col_006.name: cidr
col_006.description: Subnet CIDR in IP/prefix notation (e.g. '10.49.195.222/8'); the address shown is a representative address within the /8 block.

col_007.name: gateway_ip
col_007.description: Gateway IP address with prefix (nullable; ~18% of subnets have no gateway set).

col_010.description: IPv6 address assignment mode; only set on the two IPv6 subnets, value 'dhcpv6-stateful'. Null for IPv4 subnets.

col_011.name: subnetpool_id
col_011.description: UUID of the subnet pool the subnet's addresses are allocated from. Entirely null in this dataset, so the meaning rests on the column's position in the Neutron subnets schema; an alternative reading (some other nullable reference) cannot be ruled out from the data alone.

col_012.name: standard_attr_id
col_012.description: Foreign key to standardattributes, giving access to shared revision/standard fields (description, timestamps, revisions); one-to-one with this table.

table.name: tags

col_001.name: standard_attr_id
col_001.description: BIGINT reference to standardattributes.id, identifying the tagged resource. In Neutron's tag table this is the primary key together with the tag string. No rows exist to confirm; inferred from declared type and the presence of the standardattributes table.

col_002.description: The tag string itself (VARCHAR, part of the composite primary key with col_001). No sample values exist to confirm; inferred from the table name and Neutron schema.

table.purpose: Neutron VMware NSX (vCNS/NSX-V) plugin table binding logical Neutron routers to NSX edge devices. table.name: vips
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron LBaaS v1 virtual IP (VIP) definitions: a load-balancer listener address on a subnet, forwarding traffic on a protocol/port to a pool of members. One row per VIP.

col_001.name: tenant_id
col_001.description: Owning project/tenant ID (32-hex Neutron tenant identifier).

col_002.name: id
col_002.description: UUID primary key of the VIP.

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Human-readable name of the VIP ('spind.layer').

col_004.name: description
col_004.description: Free-text description; always NULL in this data.

col_005.name: subnet_id
col_005.description: UUID of the Neutron subnet on which the VIP address is allocated (joins subnets.id).

col_006.name: protocol_port
col_006.description: TCP/UDP port the VIP listens on (443 = HTTPS).

col_007.name: protocol
col_007.description: Load-balancing protocol (e.g. HTTP, HTTPS, TCP).

col_008.name: pool_id
col_008.description: UUID of the backend pool this VIP forwards traffic to (joins pools.id).

col_009.name: status
col_009.description: Provisioning status of the VIP (ACTIVE, PENDING_*, ERROR...).

col_010.name: status_description
col_010.description: Optional human-readable explanation of the status; always NULL here.

col_012.name: connection_limit
col_012.description: Maximum concurrent connections allowed; -1 means unlimited.
